A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed and tested a multiple readout assay for the evaluation of the cytotoxic and hormonal activity of plant and microbial extracts.

the use of a multiple readout assay based on the differential response of three human prostate cancer cell lines (LNCaP, DU145, PC-3) to plant and fungal extracts, allows us to identify extracts with hormonal (androgen receptor agonist and antagonist) and cytotoxic activities, and to classify extracts with cytotoxic activity as cytostatic or cytotoxic.
it is possible to identify androgenic, antiandrogenic, and cytotoxic activity in plant and fungal extracts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the plant extracts we tested had a significant effect on the growth of PC3 cells.
we have shown that the use of a combination of cell lines can provide a better assessment of the activity of extracts.
the use of multiple readout systems in combination with cell line panels is an efficient approach to the discovery of new compounds with hormonal or cytotoxic activities.
